rounds.text: Garnet Construction Ltd trades at an exceptionally low price-to-earnings ratio of 2.37x and a price-to-book value of 0.66x, despite a book value of ₹ 102 against a share price of ₹ 67.2 [E1, E2]. Fundamental performance has surged dramatically, highlighted by a trailing twelve-month sales growth of 415%, profit growth of 433%, and an operating margin reaching 61% in March 2026—a monumental turnaround from -69% three years prior [E11, E15, E24]. This stellar operational momentum underpins an impressive return on capital employed of 41.0% and a return on equity of 32.2% [E6, E7]. The balance sheet remains robust and conservatively managed, featuring a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.06x with borrowings reduced to ₹ 8 Cr [E31, E32], while promoter holdings remain steadfastly anchored at 61.29% [E34]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow model suggests a massive intrinsic valuation of ₹ 1143 per share, backed by a reverse DCF calculation indicating the current price absurdly prices in negative earnings growth [E36, E38]. Conceded: [E27], [E54].

Despite headline multiples that appear cheap at a P/E of 2.37 and a price-to-book ratio of 0.66x, the business suffers from severe cash flow disconnects and poor historical returns [E1, E2]. Operating cash flow for Mar 2026 is negative at Rs -1 Cr, resulting in a poor cash conversion ratio of -0.03x against reported profits and showing that operating cash flow represents only 25% of operating profit [E27, E28, E30]. Furthermore, free cash flow sits deeper in the red at Rs -3 Cr for Mar 2026, while the company maintains high debtors stretching to 300 days [E29, E54]. The long-term earnings profile reveals weak historical quality, underscored by a 10-year median return on equity of just 8% and 5-year compounded sales growth of a meager 4% [E9, E20]. Technical and momentum indicators confirm structural weakness, with the stock trading below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages, accompanied by a historical worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -95.4% and an annualized volatility of 75.8% [E41, E44, E45]. Conceded: the company displays strong recent metrics, including a trailing twelve-month sales growth of 415%, an operating margin of 61% in Mar 2026, and a rules-based screen score of 75 out of 100 [E11, E24, E55].

Conceded: [E27], [E28], [E29], and [E54]. While the bear highlights these cash flow and working capital friction points, they completely ignore the sheer magnitude of the fundamental turnaround occurring right now [E24]. Operating margins have exploded to 61% in Mar 2026—a monumental 130 percentage point expansion from -69% three years prior—proving the business model's drastically improved profitability [E24]. This soaring profitability is driving elite capital efficiency, evidenced by a stellar 41.0% ROCE and 32.2% ROE that vastly outperform the broader sector median ROCE of just 6.1% [E6, E7, E66]. The bear's fixation on historical multi-year sales growth misses the massive inflection happening in real time, led by a staggering 415% compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months and a rules-based screen score of 75 out of 100 [E11, E55]. Furthermore, the company is almost debt-free with borrowings dropping to Rs 8 Cr, completely neutralizing solvency risk while it trades at an absurdly low 2.37 P/E and 0.66x book value [E1, E2, E32, E50].

Conceded: [E6, E7, E11, E24, E50]. The bull cites the 41.0% ROCE, 32.2% ROE, TTM sales growth of 415%, operating margin expansion to 61%, and low debt [E6, E7, E11, E24, E50], but these metrics mask a severe operational disconnect when paired with negative cash flows [E27, E28, E29] and alarmingly high debtors of 300 days [E54]. An operating cash flow of minus ₹1 Cr and free cash flow of minus ₹3 Cr in March 2026 show that soaring reported profits and margins are not converting into actual cash [E27, E28, E29]. Furthermore, screeners explicitly flag that earnings growth is decelerating and the stock trades below its 200-day moving average [E60, E61], matching a historical record of a catastrophic 95.4% peak-to-trough drawdown and 75.8% annualised volatility [E44, E45]. Finally, while the bull highlights low valuations, the company pays a 0.00% dividend yield despite reporting profits [E4, E53], leaving shareholders entirely unrewarded while enduring high working capital lockups.
